challenges.name: streaming-broken-stream
challenges.title: Is this stream finished?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the tutor's streaming incident: a hint request that the edge proxy closed half-way, and two network chunks that split a Vietnamese letter.

questions.explanation: False. In a streamed response the status line and headers are sent before the first byte of the body, so 200 only says the stream started. The proxy log shows the connection was closed by an idle timeout after 30 s, and the reader reports that as an ordinary end of the body: done is true and nothing is thrown. The only proof that the answer is complete is the gateway's final [DONE] event, which never arrived. This answer is truncated: show it as interrupted, offer a retry, and never save or cache it as done. The misconception is to read "the stream ended without an exception" as "the stream finished".

questions.question:
Two network chunks of one tutor stream, as bytes (the letter ợ is e1 bb a3 in UTF-8):
chunk 1: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 22 47 e1 bb   -> data: {"delta":"G + the first two bytes of ợ
chunk 2: a3 69 20 c3 bd 22 7d 0a 0a                                  -> the last byte of ợ, then i ý"}\n\n

Client code, run for each chunk:
const text = new TextDecoder().decode(chunk);
for (const event of text.split("\n\n")) { /* JSON.parse the data line */ }

Statement: "Two separate problems hit this event: the split letter turns into replacement characters because each chunk gets a new decoder, and neither chunk holds the whole data line; one TextDecoder used with { stream: true } plus a buffer that keeps incomplete lines for the next chunk fixes both."
questions.explanation: True. A new TextDecoder sees e1 bb at the end of chunk 1 as an incomplete character and a3 at the start of chunk 2 as an invalid byte, and replaces them with U+FFFD. Independently, splitting each chunk on blank lines assumes events never cross a chunk boundary, so chunk 1 yields the unfinished text data: {"delta":"G and JSON.parse fails. decoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true }) keeps the incomplete bytes until the next call, and a text buffer that only hands complete lines to the parser keeps the event together until its blank line arrives. The misconception is that a fetch chunk is a meaningful unit: the network can cut anywhere, even inside a character.

challenges.name: assemble-sse-stream
challenges.title: Assemble a recorded SSE stream: complete, truncated or error
challenges.description:
The CodeDev AI tutor streams hints from the gateway to the browser as Server-Sent Events. The shipped client decoded and split every network chunk on its own and saved whatever it had when the reader finished: learners got replacement characters inside Vietnamese words, and a hint cut off by a proxy timeout was saved as finished. Write assembleStream(chunks: Uint8Array[]): { status, text, error }. The chunks are the bytes of one stream, cut at arbitrary places, including inside an event, between  and 
 and inside a multi-byte character. Rules: decode the bytes as UTF-8 with one decoder for the whole stream (a character can be split between chunks). A line ends with 
; remove one  right before it. An empty line ends an event. A line starting with : is a comment and is ignored. Otherwise the field name is the text before the first colon and the value is the text after it, with one leading space removed (a line without a colon is a field with an empty value). event sets the event's name; data adds a line to the event's data; every other field (id, retry, ...) is ignored. When an event ends: if it has no data line, ignore it; its data is its data lines joined with 
; its name is the event value, or message when there was none. Then: an event named error ends the stream with status "error" and error = its data. A message whose data is exactly [DONE] ends the stream with status "complete". Any other message must be JSON for an object with a string delta: append delta to text; anything else (invalid JSON, not an object, no delta, delta not a string) ends the stream with status "error" and error "malformed event". Events with other names (ping, usage, ...) are ignored. Nothing after the end of the stream is read. If the bytes run out first, status is "truncated"; an event still waiting for its empty line is dropped, even if its data is [DONE]. text is every delta appended before the end, in every status; error is null unless status is "error". The runner rebuilds the chunks from each recording { stream, cuts } (cuts = byte offsets) and prints the list of results as JSON.
hints: What does your code still need to remember when one chunk ends and the next one has not arrived yet? List every piece of state that has to survive between two calls of the loop body.

Look at four things: TextDecoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true }), which holds back an incomplete character; a string buffer where you only take text up to the next "\n" and leave the rest for later; the current event's name and its list of data lines, which reset when an event ends; and the line after the loop, which is reached only when no done marker or error event was seen.
